sections.label: A
sections.title: Look and circle the correct words.
sections.note: Choose the word that names each picture.

questions.explanation: The picture shows jellyfish: soft sea animals with long tentacles.
The insect has two large patterned wings, so it is a butterfly.
This is a small house made for a bird: a birdhouse.

sections.label: B
sections.title: Look and write the words.
sections.note: Use the word box. One word is not needed.

questions.explanation: Number 1 points to the rabbit's ears.
Number 2 points to the rabbit's eyes.
Number 3 points to the rabbit's mouth.
Number 4 points to the rabbit's head.
Number 5 points to the rabbit's body.
Number 6 points to the rabbit's legs. Feathers is the unused word.

sections.label: C
sections.title: Listen and complete the sentences.
sections.note: Listen to Track 3.42 and write one word in each gap.

questions.explanation: Birds use their wings to fly.
Elephants and bears are mammals: they are warm-blooded and feed milk to their young.
An alligator's body is covered with scales.

sections.label: D
sections.title: Circle the correct words.
sections.note: Choose the correct subject or object pronoun.

questions.prompt: 1. Me / I am friends with Cara.
questions.explanation: I is the subject of am. Me is an object pronoun.

questions.prompt: 2. Please teach us / we how to dance.
questions.explanation: After the verb teach, use the object pronoun us.

questions.prompt: 3. Bears have fur to keep them / it warm.
questions.explanation: Bears is plural, so the matching object pronoun is them.

sections.label: E
sections.title: Look and complete the sentences. Use her, him, it, or them.
sections.note: Choose the object pronoun that matches the person, animal, or group in each picture.

questions.explanation: The girl is pointing to one boy. For one male person, use him.
The girl is pointing to a group of people. For more than one person, use them.
The girl is holding one butterfly. For one animal or thing, use it.
The girl is pointing to one woman. For one female person, use her.

sections.label: F
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order to make questions. Look at the pictures and complete the answers. Use pronouns.
sections.note: Each number has two answers: write the full question, then choose the correct pronoun.

parts.label: Full question
parts.explanation: Use Do + plural subject fish + base verb have: Do fish have gills?

parts.label: Yes, ___ have them.
parts.explanation: Fish is plural here, so use they.

parts.label: Full question
parts.explanation: Use Does + singular subject a lion + base verb have.

parts.label: No, ___ doesn't have them.
parts.explanation: A lion is one animal, so use it.

parts.label: Full question
parts.explanation: Use Do + plural subject wings + base verb help.

parts.label: Yes, ___ help them.
parts.explanation: Wings is plural, so use they.

sections.label: G
sections.title: Complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use the words in the box. One word is not needed.

questions.prompt: 1. Look! That bird has a ___. It's long and pink!
questions.explanation: A long, pink animal that a bird can eat is a worm.

questions.prompt: 2. ___ are healthy. I eat them every day.
questions.explanation: Berries are small fruits. The plural verb are matches berries.

questions.prompt: 3. Animals in nature ___ for their food.
questions.explanation: Wild animals hunt when they look for and catch food.

questions.prompt: 4. ___ grow on trees, and they aren't soft.
questions.explanation: Pinecones grow on pine trees and have a hard surface.

sections.label: H
sections.title: Look and complete the words.
sections.note: Use the picture and the given letters to complete each word.

questions.explanation: The bird is making a loud, rough sound. The verb is squawk.
The two animals are attacking each other. The verb is fight.
The animal is running away from a place. The verb is escape.

sections.label: I
sections.title: Listen and check the correct picture. Write the word.
sections.note: Each number has two answers: select picture a or b, then write the word you hear.

parts.label: Correct picture
parts.explanation: The audio describes a fierce animal. Picture a shows the fierce expression.

parts.label: Word
parts.explanation: Fierce means aggressive, strong, or frightening.

parts.label: Correct picture
parts.explanation: Picture b shows an ant carrying a leaf, which represents strength.

parts.label: Word
parts.explanation: Strong means having a lot of physical power.

parts.label: Correct picture
parts.explanation: Picture a shows the gentle animal described in the audio.

parts.label: Word
parts.explanation: Gentle means calm, kind, and not rough.

sections.label: J
sections.title: Look and read. Write True or False.
sections.note: Use the frequency chart and the key below it.

questions.explanation: Martin never plays soccer, so the statement is false.
Martin sometimes eats fruit, not usually.
Sara has two check marks for the piano, which means sometimes.

questions.prompt: 4. She hardly ever goes to the park.
questions.explanation: Sara usually goes to the park, so the statement is false.

sections.label: K
sections.title: Circle the correct words.
sections.note: Choose the adverb that matches the number of check marks in the chart.

questions.prompt: 1. Martin hardly ever / never plays the piano.
questions.explanation: The chart shows an X for Martin playing the piano. X means never.

questions.prompt: 2. He sometimes / usually goes to the park.
questions.explanation: Two check marks mean sometimes.
Sara has four check marks for eating fruit. In the chart key, four check marks mean usually.

questions.prompt: 4. She never / hardly ever plays soccer.
questions.explanation: One check mark means hardly ever.

sections.label: L
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order to make sentences.
sections.note: Write each group of words as a complete sentence.

questions.explanation: Place the frequency adverb before the main verb: I never drink milk.
Always goes before the main verb eat: They always eat lunch.
Usually goes before the main verb plays: He usually plays football.
Hardly ever goes before the main verb watches: She hardly ever watches TV.
